name: LM833 / LM833-N / LM837
tagline: Cheap, quiet (4.5 nV/√Hz, 15–16 MHz, 7 V/µs) audio dual found throughout consumer and pro gear; the NE5532's sibling.

lineage.note: Named the LM833 (TI E2E 430833). DS005218, © 2004. 1980s introduction unverified.
Own design. onsemi LM833/D Rev. 6 (Sept 2011); current 'LM833, NCV833' Rev. 8 (July 2025).
Own LM833 (SLOS481, July 2010) with NPN output stage; reportedly same die as MC33078 (E2E 1443925).
Renamed National's part LM833-N (SNOSBD8); SNOSBD8D still 'LM833', -N first in SNOSBD8E (May 2012).
LM833 merged onto the NE5532/RC4580/MC33078 die (E2E 1652528; Hackaday 3 June 2026).

part_numbers.note: TI's own design (SLOS481), PDIP-8. Now on the shared die (E2E 1652528).
TI SOIC-8 reel. Reportedly listed in PCN 20231114002.1 with NE5532AP, MC33078DR, RC4580IP.
Original National die, SNOSBD8 (Rev E, May 2012). TI product page live.
National marking, now TI LM833-N. Also LM833MM/MMX in National's order list.
Motorola brand, now onsemi. Soomal found a Motorola LM833N in a Philips CD614.
onsemi PDIP / SOIC Pb-free; discontinued per LM833/D Rev. 8 (July 2025) and Arrow.
onsemi SOIC-8 reel, 15 MHz, 10–36 V (RS). JLCPCB part C7969.
onsemi automotive (AEC-Q) version on datasheet LM833/D.
ST (ex-SGS-Thomson) second source, Doc ID 2169 Rev 3. ST product page live.
Quad; TI datasheet Rev. C (Mar 2013). LM837M listed obsolete by distributors.

key_specs.value: 16 MHz (TI LM833); 15 MHz typ / 10 min (National, onsemi)
Bipolar; TI out: 2-NPN quasi-compl.; National: NPN + VPNP

reputation.summary: A cheap, quiet audio dual aimed at 'all preamp and high level stages in PCM and HiFi systems', common in CD players, equalizers and mic preamps. GroupDIY posters find lower distortion but less drive than the NE5532; Mithat Konar (2026) reportedly says it now out-specs TI's revised NE5532. No verified sound descriptors or measurements (Self, Groner, ASR).
typical_uses: Preamp and line stages in CD and hi-fi gear
Philips CD614 CD player (Motorola LM833N, Soomal)
HiFiMan HM-601 I/V after TDA1543 DAC (TI LM833)
Graphic equalizers, tone controls and mic preamps
Op-amp rolling baseline in consumer sockets
caveats: TI 'LM833' and 'LM833-N' are different devices with different output stages; check logo and exact orderable.
TI's LM833 now shares the NE5532/MC33078/RC4580 die; newer date codes may behave differently. Cut-over undocumented.
Reported ±22→±18 V and 9→5 V/µs changes are NE5532 (SLOS075K) deltas; TI's LM833 was always ±18 V, 7 V/µs.
Lower output drive than NE5532 (forum reports); isolate capacitive loads above 50 pF (LM833-N datasheet).
onsemi LM833NG/LM833DG discontinued; LM833DR2G and NCV833DR2G appear active.

counterfeit_notes: No LM833-specific counterfeit reports; unbranded DIP listings circulate (some mislabel onsemi 'LM833NG/NOPB'). Buy authorised; check logo, orderable and date code agree. 'New' onsemi LM833NG/DG stock is surplus or suspect. NE5532-family relabelled fakes are well documented.

silicon_changes.vendor: Texas Instruments (own LM833 design) vs National Semiconductor (now sold by TI as LM833-N); onsemi (Motorola design) and other vendors also make their own LM833
silicon_changes.summary: TI sells two different LM833 devices (E2E 430833). National's original has a complementary NPN + vertical-PNP output; TI's own 2010 LM833 uses a quasi-complementary two-NPN output and reportedly shares the MC33078 die (E2E 1443925). onsemi keeps Motorola's design. TI has sold both since acquiring National in 2011.

spec_deltas.before: Complementary emitter-follower pair (NPN + vertical PNP), National LM833 / LM833-N
spec_deltas.after: Quasi-complementary, two NPN devices, TI LM833 (SLOS481)

silicon_changes.identification: TI design: LM833P/LM833DR (SLOS481). Ex-National: LM833M/MX/N with /NOPB (SNOSBD8, LM833-N). National, Motorola/onsemi and ST logos mark other dies.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Different output topology can change crossover and load-driving behaviour. No published comparison measurements.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: same pinout and similar specs, but different die and output stage.
silicon_changes.verification: Confirmed via TI E2E threads and both TI datasheets.

silicon_changes.summary: After acquiring National in 2011, TI renamed National's LM833 to LM833-N to separate it from TI's own, different-die LM833 (SLOS481). Ordering a generic 'LM833' from TI gets the TI design, not the National part the reputation was built on.
silicon_changes.identification: Product and datasheet name LM833-N (SNOSBD8); orderables keep National format (LM833M, LM833MX, LM833N + /NOPB). Plain TI 'LM833' is TI's design.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None electrically; the risk is receiving TI's different die when ordering generic 'LM833'.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: naming change only; die difference covered by the second-source entry.
silicon_changes.verification: TI LM833-N product page and SNOSBD8E list the /NOPB orderables; no NRND or obsolete status found.

part_numbers_affected: LM833P and other TI SLOS481 LM833 orderables (covered by the E2E die-merge statement; PCN listing not seen)
silicon_changes.summary: TI confirmed on E2E (1652528) that NE5532, LM833, RC4580 and MC33078 now share one RC4580-based die, part numbers unchanged, after a reported SFAB-to-RFAB move with die shrink (SFAB closure 2024–2025). Publicised by Hackaday (3 Jun 2026) and Headphonesty (Jul 2026). No LM833-specific deltas documented.
silicon_changes.identification: No datasheet revision after SLOS481B or marking change. PCN 20231114002.1 lists LM833DR in Group 1 (process migration, BOM options). 2024+ date codes probably merged die.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: Unknown for LM833. The two-NPN output may now be complementary (inference). NE5532 users in the same merge report changed behaviour.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: medium: same part number, new silicon and process; stages and protection may differ (unverified for LM833).
silicon_changes.verification: PCN 20231114002.1 Group 1 lists LM833DR, MC33078DR, RC4580IP; E2E 1652528 and Hackaday confirm the merge.

silicon_changes.summary: ON Semiconductor PCN 11528 moves the Motorola-design LM833 from the BMC fab in Mesa, AZ to ON's Tesla fab in Roznov, Czech Republic. A later Roznov 150→200 mm conversion (IPCN/FPCN23597) is not tied to LM833.
silicon_changes.identification: No marking rule separates Mesa from Roznov wafers; pre-2001/2002 date codes are probably Mesa. Later Pb-free codes: LM833DG, LM833DR2G, LM833NG.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None documented; same design moved fabs.
silicon_changes.compatibility_risk: low: same design and part numbers; only process spread within limits.
silicon_changes.verification: PCN 11528 names LM833D and LM833N; LM833DR2 not separately seen.

silicon_changes.summary: onsemi has discontinued the through-hole LM833NG and the SOIC tube LM833DG; RS lists both discontinued or no longer stocked, Octopart shows LM833NG obsolete. LM833DR2G stays active. No discontinuance PCN captured.
silicon_changes.identification: Check onsemi or distributor lifecycle status; SOIC orderables (e.g. LM833DR2G) listed active.
silicon_changes.audio_impact: None electrically; DIP rollers lose the Motorola-design LM833, leaving other vendors' dies.
silicon_changes.verification: RS and Octopart listings plus LM833/D Rev. 8 discontinued note; no FPCN or date found.

claims_confirmed: TI confirmed NE5532, LM833, RC4580 and MC33078 now share one die, part numbers unchanged: https://e2e.ti.com/support/audio-group/audio/f/audio-forum/1652528/ne5532-ne5532-lm833-rc4580-and-mc33078-all-now-the-same-die
Hackaday reported the merge on 3 June 2026: https://hackaday.com/2026/06/03/texas-instruments-changes-the-ne5532-and-others-into-incompatible-versions/
Headphonesty (July 2026): RC4580-derived design with NPN inputs and complementary output: https://www.headphonesty.com/2026/07/industry-trusted-op-amp-rebuilt-boards-failing/

LM833 and LM833-N are different devices; TI used NPN output and renamed National's part: https://e2e.ti.com/support/audio-group/audio/f/audio-forum/430833/lm833-and-lm833-n-clarification-on-data-sheet-differences-sought
E2E reply: MC33078 and LM833 appear to be the same die: https://e2e.ti.com/support/audio-group/audio/f/audio-forum/1443925/mc33078-are-the-specs-the-same-as-lm833
SLOS481B (July 2010, revised Oct 2014) states 16 MHz GBW: https://www.mouser.com/datasheet/2/405/slos481b-521846.pdf
onsemi LM833DR2G listed at 15 MHz, 10–36 V: https://ie.rs-online.com/web/p/op-amps/1629355
PCN 20240429005.1 involves a die change from the RFAB process change: https://www.mouser.com/PCN/Texas_Instruments_PCN20240429005.1_Change_Notification.pdf
PCN 20231114002.1 reportedly lists LM833DR, RC4580IP, MC33078DR, NE5532AP: https://mm.digikey.com/Volume0/opasdata/d220001/medias/docus/5726/PCN20231114002.1.pdf
GroupDIY: LM833 has lower distortion but lower output drive than 5532: https://groupdiy.com/threads/lm833-vs-5532.3360/
TI document viewer still heads the LM833 datasheet 'SLOS481B July 2010 – October 2014'; Rev B follows Rev A (August 2010): https://ti.com/document-viewer/LM833/datasheet/revision_history

PCN 20231114002.1 Group 1 (process migration & BOM option qualification) lists LM833DR, RC4560IP, RC4580IP, TL5580IPWR, MC33078DR: https://e2e.ti.com/cfs-file/__key/communityserver-discussions-components-files/6/PCN20231114002.1.pdf
